# Kspec Automation Session - Task Work

**Session ID:** `01KJJYHWH08599J074BXW0JH58`
**Iteration:** 1 of 40
**Mode:** Automated (no human in the loop)


### Current State

> **Truncated** (95498 bytes). Fetch full data:
> ```
> kspec session start --json
> ```
>
> Summary: `{}`

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
$kspec-task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

The `_sid` closure variable in the `on('update')` handler captures the session ID correctly, but there is no cleanup of old listeners when starting a new session.\n\nThe Codex review on PR #484 identified that the shared mutable `sessionIterationMap` approach is fragile — a session-scoped listener pattern would be more robust.\n\n**Where**:\n- `src/cli/commands/ralph.ts` line 1061 — `sessionIterationMap` declaration\n- `src/cli/commands/ralph.ts` lines 1305-1337 — the `on('update')` handler that uses `sessionIterationMap.get(_sid)` for iteration lookup\n- `src/cli/commands/ralph.ts` line 1369 — where new sessions are registered in the map\n\n**How**:\nTwo approaches (pick one):\n\n1. **Session-scoped listeners** (recommended): Instead of one persistent `on('update')` handler, register a new listener per ACP session that captures the iteration number in its closure. Remove the old listener when the session ends or a new one starts. This eliminates the shared mutable map entirely.\n\n2. **Cleanup old sessions**: When starting a new ACP session, remove the previous session's entry from `sessionIterationMap` and call `agent.client.off('update', oldHandler)` to prevent stale callbacks. Less clean but simpler delta.\n\nBoth approaches should also ensure the translator is reset between iterations (it already creates a fresh translator per retry, but verify per-iteration reset).\n\n**Done when**:\n- Late updates from a previous ACP session are attributed to the correct iteration (the one that created that session)\n- No shared mutable state for iteration tracking — either session-scoped closures or explicit cleanup\n- Existing event logging tests still pass\n- Event log entries show correct iteration numbers even when sessions overlap",
